exercises.question: In formal mediation minutes, why is «La portavoz aclaró ayer que la moratoria sigue vigente hoy» grammatically sound alongside «La portavoz sostuvo que en la ronda anterior se había desbloqueado el diálogo»?
options: Because an offer or state that remains active at the moment of reporting can stay in the present, whereas an action completed before the past session shifts to the pluperfect
Because the reporting verb in the first sentence never permits past tenses or conditional forms inside subordinate noun clauses in formal Spanish writing
Because the time adverb meaning 'yesterday' obligatorily requires the present indicative in every subordinate clause across Latin American administrative prose
Because abstract feminine nouns denoting temporary suspensions block tense backshifting whenever they appear immediately after the conjunction «que»
